newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: ATHLETICS-GEBRESELASSIE SAYS IT IS HIS DUTY TO RUN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-GEBRESELASSIE SAYS IT IS HIS DUTY TO RUN.

text.p: Ethiopian Olympic 10,000 metres champion Haile Gebreselassie said on Tuesday he had decided to compete in the world championships in Athens because it was a national duty.
"In Athens I carry the national banner, represent my country and lead the Ethiopian team. So despite the difficult track situation I am likely to face I have decided to participate," he told Reuters.
"I am in top form and well prepared," he added.

Two weeks ago, Gebreselassie, who set a world record in the 10,000 metres at Oslo's Bislett stadium earlier this year, said he was pulling out of the world championships because the Athens track was too hard for long-distance runners.

Gebreselassie said it favoured sprinters and was similar to the track at last year's Atlanta Olympics where he said he suffered cut and injured feet. But he changed his mind last weekend and said he would run.

Ethiopian national athletic coach Wolde Meskel Kostire said Ethiopia's Athletics Federation had received assurances from the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) that the track at Athens would be improved for the championships, which open on Friday.
